seoTitle: How to Insert a Watermark in Google Docs (2026)
metaDescription: The watermark option moved in Google Docs — here's how to quickly find it and insert a text (Draft) or logo image watermark properly.
intro: If you've gone looking for the watermark option in Google Docs and come up empty, you're not imagining it — Google quietly relocated the feature, and the spot where longtime users expect to find it under Insert no longer shows it the same way. This guide covers a fast trick using the Help menu to jump straight to the tool, then walks through the actual Watermark panel: adding a "DRAFT" text stamp or a logo image, and adjusting its formatting and transparency so it looks intentional rather than like a mistake.

steps.heading: Understand why it looks like it's gone
steps.body: The watermark tool hasn't been removed from Google Docs — Google shifted where it sits in the menu structure, which is exactly the kind of small change that throws off anyone who's added a watermark before and expects it in the same place. Knowing that going in saves you from assuming the feature was dropped entirely.

steps.heading: Open your document
steps.body: Start from Google Drive with the document you want to watermark. Right-clicking a file gives you the full context menu — Open with, Download, Rename, Share, and more — and selecting it opens the doc in the Docs editor, where the watermark tool lives inside the top menu bar rather than in Drive itself.

image.caption: Right-clicking a document in Google Drive brings up the full file menu — this is just how you get into the doc before touching the watermark tool itself.

steps.heading: Use the Help menu as a shortcut
steps.body: Rather than hunting through Insert submenus, click Help in the top menu bar and choose Search the menus (or use the Option+/ shortcut). Typing "watermark" here jumps you directly to the option regardless of which submenu Google has currently filed it under, which makes this the most reliable way to find it after a menu reshuffle like this one.

image.caption: The Help menu, with Search the menus at the top — typing what you're looking for here skips the guesswork of digging through Insert's submenus.

steps.heading: Open the Watermark panel
steps.body: Selecting Watermark opens a side panel on the right with two tabs, Image and Text. The Text tab includes an Insert text field, a Formatting section for font and style, a Transparency slider, and Placement options for Diagonal or Horizontal. This panel is where every setting for the watermark lives, so leave it open while you build the watermark out in the next step.

image.caption: The Watermark panel with its Image and Text tabs, an empty Insert text field, and controls for formatting, transparency, and diagonal or horizontal placement.

steps.heading: Add and format your text watermark
steps.body: With the Text tab selected, type your watermark text into the Insert text field — "DRAFT" is the classic choice, but any short label works. Pick a font under Formatting (Impact is a solid choice for a bold, legible stamp) and drag the Transparency slider down toward 0% if you want the text to appear more solid rather than faded into the background. Diagonal placement is selected by default and tends to read most clearly across a full page of text; Horizontal is there if you'd rather the watermark run straight across.

image.caption: Typing text into the watermark field with Impact formatting applied and transparency pulled down to make the stamp more solid, Diagonal placement selected.

steps.heading: Switch to a logo image watermark
steps.body: If you'd rather stamp a company logo than a text label, click the Image tab at the top of the same panel instead of Text — it swaps the field for an upload option where you can select a file from your computer or Drive. The same Transparency and Placement controls carry over, so you can scale a logo down to something subtle in the background rather than something that competes with the page's actual content. Use Remove watermark, visible at the bottom of the panel once one is applied, if you want to clear it and start over.

faq.question: Why can't I find the watermark option in Google Docs anymore?
faq.answer: Google relocated the watermark feature within its menu structure, so it's still available but not in the exact spot longtime users remember.

faq.question: Is there a shortcut to find it faster?
faq.answer: Yes — open the Help menu and choose Search the menus (or press Option+/), then type "watermark" to jump straight to the option no matter which submenu it's currently filed under.

faq.question: Can I use both a text and image watermark at once?
faq.answer: No, the panel's Image and Text tabs are separate options — applying one replaces the other, so you'll need to choose whichever type fits the document.

faq.question: Does the watermark show when I export to PDF?
faq.answer: Yes, a watermark added through this tool carries over when you download or export the document as a PDF.

faq.question: How do I remove a watermark once it's added?
faq.answer: Reopen the Watermark panel the same way you found it, and click Remove watermark at the bottom of the panel to clear it.
